desc:
Drupal updates and security patches keep your site safe, stable and supported. Ecom Swift LLC takes a backup, applies core and module updates on a staging copy, fixes what breaks, and updates the live site once you approve.

## Why do Drupal updates and security patches matter?

Drupal updates matter because most attacks on websites use weaknesses that are already known and already fixed in a newer release. The Drupal community publishes security advisories for core and for contributed modules, and a site that never updates stays exposed to every one of them. Updates also bring bug fixes and compatibility with newer hosting software.

An out of date site rarely fails loudly. It keeps working until the day it is attacked, or until a hosting change breaks it, and by then the jump to the current version is large.

## What goes wrong when updates are put off

Delay makes each update bigger and riskier. A site that is one release behind updates in minutes. A site that is many releases behind may have modules that no longer work with each other, a theme that relies on removed features and custom code that needs rewriting.

There is also a plain business cost. If the site is compromised, you may lose content, send spam under your name or be flagged by search engines and browsers. Recovering takes far more time than regular care would have.

## How a careful update protects your results

A careful update protects what the site already earns. Visitors keep seeing working pages, forms keep sending enquiries and editors keep publishing. Testing on a copy first means a broken layout or a failed form is found and fixed before any visitor sees it.

A written report of what changed also helps. If something looks different next week, you and your developer can check exactly what was updated and when.

## What a good update round includes

- A full backup of files and database before any change.
- A staging copy of the live site for all testing.
- Core updated to the latest release that suits your site.
- Pending security patches applied to core and modules.
- Contributed module updates, checked for compatibility.
- Fixes for problems the updates expose, in the theme or settings.
- A check of broken links and not found pages.
- A review of the error log for hidden warnings.
- Cleanup of unused modules, cron and file permission checks in larger rounds.
- A clear report listing every change.

## What we do

We copy your site to staging and take a backup of the live version. We apply core updates and the security patches first, then the module updates, running the database updates Drupal requires. After each step we click through key pages, test forms and log in as an editor.

When something breaks, we fix it on staging. The Basic package covers one round of core updates and security patches. Standard adds all module updates and a set of related fixes. Premium adds a deeper cleanup, server settings review and a short checklist your team can follow in future. When you approve staging, we update the live site at a quiet moment and confirm it works.

This is a fixed starter round, not a monthly plan. If you want regular care afterwards, we quote that separately.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Keep a recent backup stored away from the web server.
- Test updates on a copy before the live site.
- Update on a regular schedule, not only after a scare.
- Remove modules you no longer use.
- Keep a note of any custom changes made to core or contributed code.

**Avoid:**
- Editing core or contributed module files directly.
- Running updates on the live site with no backup.
- Ignoring security advisories because the site seems fine.
- Letting several major releases pile up.
- Updating during your busiest hours.

## Who this is for

This suits an organization whose Drupal site was built a while ago and has not been touched since. It also suits a small team without a developer, and a business that has received a warning from its host about an old version. If your last update date is a guess, this is the right place to start.

## What we need from you

Send the site address and tell us where it is hosted, and whether you already have a staging copy. We need developer or administrator access set up as a collaborator or staff user, and we never ask for passwords. Tell us about any pages or forms that must never break. We will confirm the plan and the time of the live update with you first.
